Detect outbreak onsets for every location of a MOSAIC config

Source: R/est_outbreak_onsets.R
est_outbreak_onsets.Rd

Builds each location's weekly series of reported suspected cases from a MOSAIC config and runs calc_outbreak_onset on it. Weeks are the complete Monday-to-Sunday weeks of the config's daily window (partial edge weeks are dropped); a week is reported when all seven of its days are, and its count is their sum.

Usage

est_outbreak_onsets(
  config,
  method = c("growth", "growth_sensitive", "zheng"),
  mode = c("retrospective", "realtime"),
  source = c("smooth", "raw"),
  imputed = c("unreported", "keep"),
  population = NULL,
  locations = NULL,
  n_cores = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

config

A MOSAIC config (e.g. config_default) with date_start, date_stop, location_name, reported_cases and, optionally, reported_tier.

method

"growth" (default), "growth_sensitive" or "zheng"; see calc_outbreak_onset.

mode

"retrospective" (default) or "realtime".

source

What the growth rules work on: "smooth" (default) or "raw" (the reported counts); see calc_outbreak_onset.

imputed

"unreported" (default) treats tier-3 days as unreported; "keep" counts them.

population

NULL (default) reads param_N_population_size.csv from get_paths()$MODEL_INPUT; or a data frame with columns iso_code, date, population. Each week takes the latest value on or before its first day (the earliest value for weeks before the first date).

locations

ISO codes to run (default: every location of the config).

n_cores

Number of locations to run at once (default 1: one after another); capped at the number of locations and of cores. See Parallel runs.

...

Rule settings passed to calc_outbreak_onset.

Value

A data frame of the columns of calc_outbreak_onset with iso_code first and imputed_share added: the share of the config's reported cases within two weeks of the onset that come from imputed days. The attribute "series" stacks the locations' weekly series with an iso_code column.

Details

Imputed days (reported_tier 3, every modelled disaggregation method, e.g. AI fourier_* reconstructions of annual totals and inferred_zero absences) are treated as unreported by default, as est_epidemic_peaks does: a Fourier reconstruction has a seasonal peak every year by construction. With imputed = "keep" they count as reported, which reproduces the series the onset handoff was tuned on. WHO multi-week reports spread over their weeks (tier 2) count as reported either way.

Parallel runs. Locations are independent, so n_cores > 1 runs them in forked worker processes (parallel::mclapply, each worker taking the next location when it finishes one, with single-threaded BLAS). This pays off in real time, where the growth rules refit the smooth every week: on a laptop a country takes about 40 seconds (up to 75), so the 40 countries of config_default take about 24 minutes one after another and under 4 minutes on 8 cores. The full-series rules and the Zheng rule take under a second per country. The result is identical to a serial run, and so are warnings and errors: a location's warnings are raised with its ISO code in front, and the first location (in locations order) that fails stops the call with its ISO code. Windows cannot fork, so there the locations run one after another, with a warning.

See also

calc_outbreak_onset

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")
onsets <- est_outbreak_onsets(config_default)
onsets_rt <- est_outbreak_onsets(config_default, mode = "realtime", locations = c("MOZ", "ETH"))
onsets_rt_all <- est_outbreak_onsets(config_default, mode = "realtime", n_cores = 8)
onsets_raw <- est_outbreak_onsets(config_default, mode = "realtime", source = "raw")
} # }
